rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Noah formula in al-Aʿrāf lacks an opening conjunction, while al-Muʾminūn and Hūd include it.
rows.anchor: لقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿrāf says they denied earlier; Yūnus adds the object pronoun “it.”
rows.anchor: فى الأعراف ﴿ كذبوا من قبل ﴾ وفى يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿrāf omits “by his magic” from Pharaoh’s claim that Moses would expel them from their land; al-Shuʿarāʾ includes it.
rows.anchor: يريد أن يخرجكم من أرضكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd has “we are in doubt” and “you call us,” whereas Ibrāhīm uses “we are” and “you call us” with different forms.
rows.anchor: وإننا لفي شك مما تدعونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yūsuf includes من after “before you”; al-Anbiyāʾ omits it.
rows.anchor: وما أرسلنا من قبلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revival formula in al-ʿAnkabūt adds مِن before “after its death”; al-Naḥl lacks the preposition.
rows.anchor: فأحيا به الأرض بعد موتها

words: لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدَ عِلْمٍۢ شَيْـًۭٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel phrase about no longer knowing after knowledge varies by the presence or omission of مِن.
rows.anchor: لكيلا يعلم من بعد علم شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥajj repeats “from grief” in the phrase about being returned to the Fire; al-Sajda omits that phrase.
rows.anchor: كلما أرادوا أن يخرجوا منها من غم أعيدوا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Naml begins the command to throw the staff with وألق; al-Qaṣaṣ has وأن ألق.
rows.anchor: فى النمل ﴿ وألق عصاك ﴾ وفى القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAnkabūt says “when our messengers came to Lot” with أن, while Hūd omits it.
rows.anchor: ولما أن جاءت رسلنا لوطا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muʾmin says the Hour is certainly coming with لآتية; Ṭā Hā has آتية.
rows.anchor: فى سورة المؤمن ﴿ إن الساعة لآتية ﴾ وفى طه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Naḥl says “those they call upon besides God,” while al-Aʿrāf uses “besides Him.”
rows.anchor: والذين يدعون من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muʾminūn names Moses and his brother Aaron; Ghāfir omits the brother.
rows.anchor: موسى وأخاه هارون بآياتنا وسلطان مبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm uses a conjunction before “they slaughtered your sons” because it lists distinct trials after recalling God’s days and blessings; al-Baqara’s following phrase explains “afflicting you.” Al-Aʿrāf’s “killing” echoes Pharaoh’s threat.
rows.anchor: واللائق أن يعدد امتحانهم تعديدا يؤذن بصدق الجمع عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge begins by asking humans and jinn together to produce a Qurʾān like this one.
rows.anchor: قل لئن اجتمعت الإنس والجن على أن يأتوا بمثل هذا القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge narrows to ten fabricated sūras; “fabricated” removes the excuse that they lack knowledge of its past reports and stories.
rows.anchor: قل فأتوا بعشر سور مثله مفتريات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After they fail the ten-sūra challenge, the Qurʾān reduces it to one comparable sūra to intensify their inability.
rows.anchor: فردهم من العشر إلى سورة واحدة من مثله مبالغة فى التعجيز لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assurance “you will never do so” intensifies the challenge and culminates in a warning to fear the Fire.
rows.anchor: فإن لم تفعلوا ولن تفعلوا

rows.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
rows.claim: Al-Walīd, one of Quraysh’s leading eloquent men, judged that the Qurʾān was neither poetry, magic, madness, nor soothsaying.
rows.anchor: الوليد بن المغيرة لعنه الله كان سيد قريش وأحد فصحائهم لما سمعه

rows.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
rows.claim: Al-Walīd praised the Qurʾān’s sweetness and beauty, fertile lower part, fruitful upper part, and supremacy over other speech.
rows.anchor: والله إن لقوله لحلاوة وإن عليه لطلاوة وإن أسفله لمغدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says pride made al-Walīd recant his recognition and call the Qurʾān transmitted magic and human speech.
rows.anchor: ثم حملته الحمية فنكص على عقبيه وكابر حسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The operative challenge addresses humans, since jinn are not speakers of the Arabic tongue and styles in which the Qurʾān was revealed.
rows.anchor: لأن الجن ليسوا من أهل اللسان العربى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Including jinn magnifies the Qurʾān’s inimitability: even a united alliance of both communities, aiding one another, could not answer it.
rows.anchor: فإذا فرض اجتماع جميع الإنس والجن وظاهر بعضهم بعضا وعجزوا عن العارضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author likens the point to a full brother’s precedence over a paternal brother in marriage guardianship, although maternal kinship does not determine marriage.
rows.anchor: ونظيره فى الفقه تقدم والأخ الشقيق على الأخ للأب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Satan and his offspring allies despite their enmity is condemned as a bad exchange.
rows.anchor: أفتتخذونه وذريته أولياء من دوني وهم لكم عدو بئس للظالمين بدلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers are told not to take the hostile group as allies unless they migrate in God’s path.
rows.anchor: فلا تتخذوا منهم أولياء حتى يهاجروا في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Encouragement urges noble qualities: God’s praise of fighters, promised angelic reinforcements, the ban on turning away, divine victory, and believers’ greater hope.
rows.anchor: الخامس والعشرون خطاب التشجيع والتحريض وهو الحث على الاتصاف بالصفات الجميلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alongside encouragement, Qurʾānic guidance calls for prudence in war, preparation, and securing the means of defense.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء في مقابلة هذا القسم ما يراد منه الآخذ بالحزم والتأني بالحرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stories of the wicked warn through their punishments, while accounts of the blessed encourage through their reward.
rows.anchor: ما جاء في قصص الأشقياء تحذيرا لما نزل من العذاب واخبارا للسعداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition of backbiting deters through the repellent image of eating one’s dead brother’s flesh and a rebuking rhetorical question.
rows.anchor: ولا يغتب بعضكم بعضا أيحب أحدكم أن يأكل لحم أخيه ميتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image intensifies aversion by asking whether any of you would love it, then successively making the flesh human, a brother’s, and dead.
rows.anchor: ولم يقتصر على تمثيل الاعتبار باكل لحم الإنسان حتى جعله أخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The backbitten person is absent and cannot defend himself, so the author likens him to a dead person.
rows.anchor: ومنها ان المغتاب غائب وهو لايقدر على الدفع لما قيل فيه فهو كالميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Badal clarifies after an initially ambiguous noun and can also emphasize it; a whole, part, or included relation can supply the clarification.
rows.anchor: القصد به الإيضاح بعد الإبهام وهو يفيد البيان والتأكيد أما البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An explanatory badal identifies the intended referent and, by repeating the governing relation in effect, removes uncertainty about which part was meant.
rows.anchor: إذا قلت ضربت زيدا جاز أن تكون ضربت رأسه

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh says the noun is built as emphasis and behaves like an adjective in clarification, since the combined terms identify the intended person.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول سيبويه ولكنه بني الاسم تأكيدا وجرى مجرى الصفة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains that the first term prepares the construction and the pair together add emphasis and clarification beyond either alone.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول الزمخشري وإنما يذكر الآولى لتجوز التوطئة

rows.speaker: ابن السيد
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sayyid says some badal emphasizes a clear antecedent rather than removing doubt, as in “a straight path, God’s path”; Sībawayh allows this purpose.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن السيد ليس كل بدل يقصد به رفع الإشكال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike an adjective, badal is understood as repeating the governing verb or preposition, as the repeated مِن in the example shows; it still clarifies its antecedent.
rows.anchor: والفرق بينه وبين الصفة أن البدل في تقدير تكرار العامل

rows.speaker: ابن الخشاب
rows.claim: Repeating “the kingdom” instead of using a pronoun avoids the possible ambiguity of what “you grant it” would refer to.
rows.anchor: لو قال تؤتيه لأوهم أنه الآول قاله ابن الخشاب

rows.speaker: الوزير المغربي
rows.claim: Al-Wazīr al-Maghribī says “evil” is repeated so “their circle” cannot be misconstrued as referring to God.
rows.anchor: كرر السوء لانه لو قال عليهم دائرة لالتبس بأن يكون الضمير عائدا إلى الله

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib distinguishes the weakness and strength stages: early weakness is infancy, strength follows puberty, and the final weakness is old age; different wording marks distinct stages.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن الحاجب ويؤيد الغيرية التنكير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating “Qurʾān at dawn” rather than saying “it” prevents the pronoun from seeming to refer to dawn itself.
rows.anchor: وقرآن الفجر إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Every soul argues for itself” uses a repeated noun instead of a pronoun to avoid making the subject and object pronouns identical.
rows.anchor: يوم تأتي كل نفس تجادل عن نفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating “the vessel” instead of saying “from it” prevents a pronoun from implying that Joseph’s brother himself initiated its removal, which would be unbecoming.
rows.anchor: لأنه لو قيل ذلك لآوهم عود الضمير على الأخ فيصير كأن الآخ مباشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying “his vessel” could refer to Joseph, the nearest antecedent, so the explicit noun also removes that ambiguity.
rows.anchor: فلو قال من وعائه لتوهم أنه يوسف لأنه أقرب مذكور فأظهر لذلك

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib explains that angels are called barara, stronger than abrār: barara is the plural of barr, whose sense is stronger than bārr; the distinction assumes angels’ superiority.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب فخص ( 3 ) الملائكة بها ( 4 ) من حيث أنه ابلغ

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Fāris and other language scholars distinguish the plurals: إخوة for blood siblings, إخوان for friendship or religious brotherhood.
rows.anchor: قال جماعة من أهل اللغة منهم ابن فارس وحكاه أبو حاتم عن أهل البصرة

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abū Ḥātim rejects a strict split between the plurals: both إخوة and إخوان can refer to friends or kin.
rows.anchor: ثم رده بأنه يقال للأصدقاء والنسب إخوة وإخوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author endorses the broader usage: إخوة can mean believers, while إخوان can name kin; the plural forms do not map exclusively to one relation.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الصواب واشتقاق اللفظين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two terms are derived from taʾākhaytu: each brother inclines toward what the other inclines toward.
rows.anchor: كل واحد منهما يتأخى ما تأخاه الآخر أي يقصده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Comitative مع can express sharing between an object and an annexed term, as in smelling perfume together with Zayd.
rows.anchor: وقد تكون المصاحبة في الاشتراك بين المفعول وبين المضاف كقوله شممت طيبا مع زيد

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A view cited by Abū al-Fatḥ al-Qushayrī takes “with me” in Moses’ exchange with the sage as comitative; a poetic usage is also cited for consideration.
rows.anchor: نقل ذلك أبو الفتح القشيري في شرح الإلمام عن بعضهم

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says مع conveys togetherness in place, time, a relational meaning, or rank and status.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب مع تقتضي الاجتماع إما في المكان نحو هما معا في الدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مع can signify aid or presence: “with you” means supporting you; God’s being with people can mean assisting them or knowing and witnessing them.
rows.anchor: ويكون بمعنى النصرة والمعونة والحضور

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Mālik says unqualified معاً has the same meaning as جميعاً.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مالك إن معا إذا أفردت تساوى جميعا معنى

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān, citing Thaʿlab, rejects Ibn Mālik’s equation: جميعاً may allow different times, but معاً requires simultaneous action; the author calls this the sound account.
rows.anchor: ورد عليه الشيخ أبو حيان بأن بينهما فرقاء قال ثعلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most grammarians treat مع as a temporal adverb: “Zayd was with ʿAmr” means at the time ʿAmr arrived, with the time and event omitted.
rows.anchor: وهو ظرف زمان عند الأكثرين إذا قلت كان زيد مع عمرو أي زمن مجىء عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavy emphatic nūn is used for imprisonment but not the following clause to magnify the threat of imprisonment.
rows.anchor: من حيث أكدت السجن بالشدة دون ما بعده إعظاما

rows.speaker: السلف
rows.claim: The Salaf say the lām in “mothers of your wives and stepdaughters” is ambiguous: intercourse with the wife conditions the stepdaughter’s prohibition only.
rows.anchor: قول السلف في قوله تعالى ﴿ وأمهات نسائكم وربائبكم ﴾

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī’s principle is that a text is clear about its intended scope but may bear other interpretations outside that scope.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال الشافعي اللفظ بين في مقصوده ويحتمل في غير مقصوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning against hoarding gold and silver establishes the duty to pay zakāt, but does not define its amount or extend it to every quantity and kind of ornament.
rows.anchor: لا يصلح الاحتجاج بها في إيجاب الزكاة في قليل الذهب والفضة وكثيره

rows.speaker: القفال الشاشي
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl al-Shāshī says the chastity passage praises those who have relations only with spouses or owned partners; it does not specify which unions or possessions are lawful.
rows.anchor: قاله القفال الشاشي ( 1 ) وفيه نظر لما سبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author questions al-Qaffāl’s claim in light of the preceding discussion about how broad wording relates to its intended legal scope.
rows.anchor: وفيه نظر لما سبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission to eat, drink, and have marital relations on fasting nights lifts a prior restriction; it does not legalize every food, drink, or sexual act.
rows.anchor: بل مبينة لحكم جواز الأكل والشرب والمباشرة إلى الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A stepdaughter’s being raised in the husband’s home describes the usual situation, not a condition of prohibition; the later ruling names intercourse but not residence.
rows.anchor: فإن الحجر ليس بقيد عند العلماء لكن فائدة التقييد تأكيد الحكم في هذه الصورة

words: فَإِن لَّمْ تَكُونُوا۟ دَخَلْتُم بِهِنَّ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says that because the prohibition depends on combined conditions, removing any one condition should remove the whole prohibition; the reply is that the remaining part of the cause still operates.
rows.anchor: واعترض بأن الحرمة إذا كانت بالمجموع فالحل يثبت بانتفاء المجموع

words: فَإِن لَّمْ تَكُونُوا۟ دَخَلْتُم بِهِنَّ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit no-intercourse clause prevents readers from treating intercourse as merely another customary detail like a stepdaughter’s residence in the home.
rows.anchor: فائدته ألا يتوهم أن قيد الدخول خرج مخرج الغالب لا مخرج الشرط

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority hold that a qualifier describing a prevalent custom does not restrict the rule to that description.
rows.anchor: إذا خرج مخرج الغالب فلا تقييد فيه عند الجمهور

rows.speaker: إمام الحرمين
rows.claim: Imām al-Ḥaramayn, ʿIzz al-Dīn ibn ʿAbd al-Salām, and al-ʿIrāqī argue that a stated qualifier can indicate a ruling for the otherwise unmentioned case, since a common attribute could have been left unstated.
rows.anchor: خلافا لإمام الحرمين والشيخ عز الدين بن عبد السلام والعراقي حيث قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “For fear of poverty” is another description framed by the prevalent motive for killing children.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى ﴿ ولا تقتلوا أولادكم خشية إملاق ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pledge in lieu of a scribe is recommended for travel because lack of a trustworthy scribe and witnesses is more usual there; the rule is not limited to travel.
rows.anchor: وجوزوا أن الرهن لا يختص بالسفر لكن ذكر لأن فقد الكاتب يكون فيه غالبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing the area around the sanctuary as blessed signals, a fortiori, that the sanctuary itself is blessed.
rows.anchor: فنبه على حصول البركة فيه من باب أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on even saying “uff” to parents conveys the broader ban on insulting or striking them through the verse’s purpose of honoring parents.
rows.anchor: كما في آية التأفيف فإنا نعلم أن الآية إنما سيقت لاحترام الوالدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This contextual implication is not real qiyās, since the broader meaning is understood from the wording without separate inference or reflection.
rows.anchor: ما يتأخر من نظم الكلام وما يتقدم فهمه على اللفظ ويقترن به لا يكون قياسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a text states a rule with a qualifier, the unstated case may either have a different rule or the same rule, depending on the context.
rows.anchor: وقد ( 4 ) يحكم على الشيء مقيدا بصفة ثم قد يكون ما سكت عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restricting the prohibition to wives of biological sons signals that wives of foster sons are permitted; it does not permit relations with enslaved women owned by one’s sons.
rows.anchor: وحلائل أبنائكم الذين من أصلابكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s list implies that displaying adornment before other men is forbidden, but its list does not establish the rule for kin related through nursing.
rows.anchor: لا جناح عليهن في آبائهن ولا أبنائهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hunting penalty also applies to accidental killing: killing is a form of damage, and damage occurs both intentionally and by mistake.
rows.anchor: فإن القتل إتلاف والإتلاف عمده وخطؤه فيستدل به على أن التعمد ليس بشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One method keeps each general text tied to its apparent purpose: the ban on combining sisters states what is lawful or forbidden, while the permission concerning owned women removes blame for that circumstance.
rows.anchor: وأن تجمعوا بين الأختين إلا ما قد سلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further method distinguishes a rule attached to a word’s meaning from one attached to its name, allowing “others than you” to mean another tribe rather than another faith.
rows.anchor: أن يكون تخصيص أحد الإستعمالين على لفظ تعلق بمعناه والآخر باسمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Explicitly stating that trade is lawful outweighs an apparent implication that the Friday command to leave trade invalidates a sale.
rows.anchor: ترجيح ما يعلم بالخطاب ضرورة على ما يعلم منه ظاهرا

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr says revelation does not genuinely conflict with itself or reason; because God alone creates, تخلقون means “fabricate a lie” and Jesus’s خلق means “shape” clay.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو بكر في ( التقريب ) لا يجوز

rows.speaker: عز الدين
rows.claim: ʿIzz al-Dīn rejects the need to supply “effective warning”: warning is literal for those who fear the Hour because it produces its effect, and metaphorical for those who do not.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ عز الدين ولاحاجة إلى هذا لان فعل وافعل اذا لم يترتب عليه مطاوعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “do not approach this tree lest you become wrongdoers,” the verb after ف may be jussive, extending the prohibition to becoming wrongdoers, or subjunctive, expressing the consequence.
rows.anchor: يحتمل إن يكون ما بعد الفاء مجزوما ويحتمل إن يكون منصوبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “do not mix truth with falsehood and conceal truth,” jussive تكتموا can prohibit both acts; subjunctive can prohibit combining them. The author prefers the first reading.
rows.anchor: فإنه يحتمل إن يكون تكتموا مجزوما فهو مشترك مع الأول في حرف النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the clause about neither touching a woman nor assigning her a dowry, تفرضوا is read jussive with تمسوهن; another view makes it subjunctive and reads أو as “except if.”
rows.anchor: تفرضوا مجزوم عطفا على تمسوهن
